transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s probably not anything dramatic, but what finally pushed me to make the appointment is this constant tightness. My neck and shoulders are tense most of the time, and even my jaw feels clenched, like I’m bracing myself for something bad to happen. It can be when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to relax watching TV at night. I wasn’t sure if that’s the sort of thing I should come in for, but it’s been hard to ignore.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things?

Yes… I suppose I do. I try not to make a big thing of it, because a lot of it feels like normal adult responsibilities, you know? But my mind does keep jumping around—from whether the contractors might’ve missed something in the house, to whether my lesson plans are starting to slip, whether the robotics kids are falling behind… and then I start wondering if I’m letting my wife and family down by not keeping everything under control. 

I don’t know if that counts as “a lot,” but it feels like it’s there more than I’d like.
Did these worries and the constant tension start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

I think so, yes. It wasn’t some huge trauma or anything, but about seven months ago a pipe burst at the house, and the remodeling after that really threw everything into chaos. Since then, the worry and the tension just sort of… stayed. I kept thinking it would settle once the house did, but it hasn’t really.
Do you feel the worry is now about many different parts of your life, not just the house repairs?

Yes… I think that’s fair. I wish I could say it was just the house, because that would make more sense, but it’s sort of spread out now.

My mind keeps jumping from whether the contractors missed something, to whether my lesson plans aren’t as solid as they should be, or whether the robotics students are getting behind. And then I’ll start thinking maybe I’m disappointing my wife or my family because I’m not keeping everything under control. It sounds a bit much when I say it out loud, but yes, it’s not just the repairs anymore.
When the worrying starts, do you find it hard to stop or control it?

Yes… I mean, I can usually keep functioning, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely falling apart. But it is hard to stop once it gets going.

I’ll tell myself, “Just focus on the class in front of you,” and I do try. But then one small thing—like remembering a late invoice, or worrying a student is falling behind—sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. And even when I know it’s not helpful, I can’t seem to shut it down easily. Does that make sense?
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I do sleep, so I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Some nights are better than others, I suppose. Are you asking about falling asleep, or waking up during the night?
Do you have trouble falling asleep?

I’m… not really sure. I wouldn’t say it’s every night or anything dramatic. Sometimes I lie there longer than I’d like, but I don’t know if that counts as “trouble falling asleep,” exactly.

I suppose there are nights where it takes me a while to settle, but I can usually get to sleep eventually. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have these worries been present on most days for at least six months?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but it’s been about seven months now.

It started around when that pipe burst at home and the remodeling kind of threw everything into chaos. Since then, it’s been there most days, I’d say. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly because of the house-remodeling stress, or does it now feel separate from that?

I think it started with the remodeling, yes, but… it doesn’t feel like it stays neatly in that box anymore.

My mind will jump from, you know, whether the contractors missed something in the house, to whether my lesson plans are slipping, or whether the robotics kids are getting behind. And then I’ll start thinking I’m disappointing my wife or my family because I’m not keeping everything under control.

I’m not sure if that answers it properly, but it feels like it’s spread beyond just the house.
Do you feel your level of worry is more than most people would have after something like the house damage and remodeling?

I suppose… yes, maybe it is more than what most people would have. I don’t love saying that, because the house situation was genuinely stressful.

But my mind keeps jumping around. It’ll start with whether the contractors missed something, and then suddenly I’m worrying that my lesson plans are slipping, or that the robotics kids are falling behind, or that I’m letting my wife and family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.

So… yes, I think it’s probably more than it needs to be. Does that make sense?
Has this worry been interfering with your work or your life at home?

A bit, yes. I mean, I’m still functioning, and I don’t want to make it sound like everything has fallen apart, but I have started falling behind on lesson prep and grading more than I’m comfortable with.

At home, or I guess outside of work too, I’ve had to step back from some of the community-theater stuff I usually help manage. I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore. I’m not proud of that, but… yes, it has been interfering some.
